cases.title: The editor's own defaults for a transform are admitted.
cases.notes: The defect this suite exists for. The reference's validator refused its own defaults (the blank row's `key` is required) until 0.82.0, and the Python and PHP ports declared only a REQUIRED `expression`, so every node dropped from the editor was refused. `fields` now declares `skipBlankRows`: a row whose every field is blank is an unfilled placeholder.

cases.title: Expression mode with the blank default row still present is admitted.
Fields mode with filled-in rows and a trailing blank row is admitted.
A row that is an empty object is blank, and admitted.
cases.notes: PHP decodes `{}` to `[]`, the same value as an empty list, so the PHP port treats an empty array row as the blank object it came from.

cases.title: A mode the schema does not list is refused.
A row with a value and no key is refused: the executor would drop that value silently.
cases.notes: This is why the blank-row rule is 'every field blank' rather than 'key blank'. Skipping on a blank key alone would admit a configured value that never reaches the output -- field loss with no signal. Rust ran this row from 0.43.0: fancy-flow-rs validate_config did not walk repeater rows before, so it admitted this config too.

cases.title: `fields` that is not a list is refused.

skip.rust: fancy-flow-rs validate_config is deliberately shallow (required fields, select options, and a repeater row's required cells) and does not type-check values or rows

cases.title: A `fields` row that is not an object is refused.

skip.rust: fancy-flow-rs validate_config is deliberately shallow (required fields, select options, and a repeater row's required cells) and does not type-check values or rows

cases.title: An `expression` that is not a string is refused, whichever mode is selected.

skip.rust: fancy-flow-rs validate_config is deliberately shallow (required fields, select options, and a repeater row's required cells) and does not type-check values or rows

cases.title: A row whose key is only whitespace but which has a value is refused, like an empty key: the executor trims the key and would drop that value.
cases.notes: Maipa's config, verbatim, reported against the published TS 0.82.0 and PHP 0.65.0. Validators compared the key with an exact empty string while every executor TRIMS it, so this was admitted, imported cleanly and then ran as a passthrough with the value silently gone. Admission must judge blankness exactly as the executor does. ASCII spaces only: the runtimes' trims agree on ASCII and differ at the edges of Unicode, which this row is not about.

cases.title: A row whose key is only whitespace and whose value is empty is a blank row, and admitted.
cases.notes: The trimmed judgement cuts both ways: a whitespace-only key is blank for skipping the row too, so a row with nothing configured stays a placeholder -- as the editor's untouched default (0001) does. Before 0.43.0's fix the reference refused this row ('Value is required') while running it as nothing.

cases.title: A key padded with whitespace around real text is admitted.
cases.notes: Guards the fix for 0010 from overreaching: trimming decides whether a key is BLANK, and a padded key is not. At run time its value lands under the trimmed key (flow/graph-runs 0042).
